attempts.summary: Implemented VLAN segmentation over the shared node1-node2-node3 link using an Ansible playbook run from node4 (the ansible-controller managed node). node2 was placed on VLAN 10 (10.10.10.0/24) and node3 on VLAN 20 (10.10.20.0/24) via 802.1q sub-interfaces on their shared trunk NIC (enp8s0), configured with NetworkManager (community.general.nmcli). node1 (VyOS) was configured with matching eth1.10/eth1.20 sub-interfaces and routes traffic between the VLANs. End-to-end ping between node2 and node3 succeeds via node1 (TTL=63 confirms one router hop). The playbook is fully idempotent (repeat runs report changed=0). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all four managed nodes: captured baseline boot IDs and healthy state, restarted each node one at a time via native reboot with an acknowledgement returned before disconnect, confirmed changed boot identity via /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, and verified full recovery of VLAN interfaces, routes, and cross-VLAN connectivity after each restart — including a final idempotent Ansible re-run from the restarted control node (node4) proving the desired state persisted through every reboot.
